elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Client owns all deliverables and work product created for Client under this Agreement, including all results of the Support Services".

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: "...and TrueLink hereby assigns such deliverables and work product to Client." Present-tense operative assignment, not an agreement to assign.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 2(d): "Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface"; the new clause is consistent, granting only a licence to "TrueLink Intellectual Property embedded in such deliverables".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to any TrueLink Intellectual Property embedded in such deliverables and work product."

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: "Client retains all right, title and interest in Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property and Credit Data." This covers both data categories the Agreement uses for Client-side data (Client Content and Credit Data).

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 8(d) as amended: "nonexclusive worldwide right and license to process, upload, display, copy and store Credit Data solely to provide the Hosting and Support Services to Client". The distribute/disseminate/license/resell/exploit rights that defeated this element are deleted; remaining verbs are service-delivery acts.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: "No intellectual property will be jointly owned by the parties."

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 2(d) preserves TrueLink's ownership of the Interface, and the inserted clause reserves TrueLink Intellectual Property (licensing only what is embedded); nothing strips generic tools/know-how.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Customer takes outright ownership of deliverables, and the residual embedded-IP licence is expressly "perpetual".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Embedded-IP licence expressly "irrevocable"; ownership of the deliverables themselves is not revocable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is qualified only as "perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free"; no territorial word appears. To close the fallback level the drafter would need to add "worldwide" to that grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Client owns the deliverables and work product outright, which carries use and modification rights; the embedded TrueLink IP licence is unrestricted as to purpose.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Ownership covers the deliverables, but the licence to embedded TrueLink Intellectual Property contains no express sublicensing right, so onward sublicensing of deliverables containing TrueLink IP is not expressly permitted.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 8(d) limits the Credit Data licence to processing, uploading, displaying, copying and storing "solely to provide the Hosting and Support Services to Client".

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all nine preferred elements are met in operative language, so the redline may be accepted as drafted even though the fallback checklist is not independently complete (no "worldwide" and no sublicence right on the embedded TrueLink IP grant).

The Section 8(d) edit removes exactly the offending exploitation verbs (use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit) and substitutes a service-delivery purpose limitation; the heading, the nonexclusive/worldwide framing and the Non-Competition Agreement cross-reference are retained, so nothing outside the target element is disturbed.

The inserted Client Ownership clause is a concise insertion filling a genuine gap (the Agreement contained no ownership/assignment, data-retention or anti-joint-ownership language) and adds no survival tail, expense, remedy or procedure. The added words "Client's Intellectual Property" and "including all results of the Support Services" are declaratory and within the rule's scope, so minimality is preserved, but they are the only clauses that could be trimmed if the counterparty pushes back.

Intent is preserved: Section 2(d)'s Interface ownership is untouched and consistent with the new grant; no cross-reference is orphaned. Note that the 31-day/archiving mechanics in the Credit Data definition existed to delimit TrueLink's downstream data use — they remain operable as a definitional filter, but flag internally that their commercial purpose is diminished once the licence is narrowed.

Drafting check before sending: confirm "Client Content", "Client's Intellectual Property", "TrueLink Intellectual Property" and "Hosting and Support Services" match defined terms used elsewhere in the Agreement; if any are undefined, replace with the defined equivalents (e.g. "Client Proprietary Information", "Support Services") to avoid an undefined-term defect.

Optional hardening (not required for preferred completeness): add "worldwide" and a right to sublicense to the embedded TrueLink IP licence so the clause also clears the fallback checklist if TrueLink resists the assignment.
